story.headline: ASIO and the AFP open Australia's $74 million Counter Terrorism Online Centre in Sydney to monitor high-risk online spaces
story.why: Opens in Sydney today, Fri 13 Nov 2026; reported by AAP (12 Nov, afternoon AEDT) and ABC News (posted 5:00am AEDT 13 Nov). Australian relevance 3/3 (national security, young people online), debate 2.5/3 (protection vs civil liberties and oversight), measurable 1.5/2 ($74M over two years; AFP study: all 55 youth terror cases radicalised wholly or partly online), timeliness 2/2 (+1 under 12 hours). Beat Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation (8: huge US story, thin Australian angle, allegation-heavy) and the Productivity Commission regional airfares interim report (7).

discussion_question: If ASIO and the AFP now watch the chat rooms where teens are radicalised, is that protection or overreach?

linkedin.post:
Every one of the 55 youth terror cases the AFP studied involved radicalisation wholly or partly online.

From today, a $74 million Counter Terrorism Online Centre in Sydney puts ASIO and the AFP together to monitor high-risk online spaces. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke says the watch on extremists now extends to the chat room. Criminologists have warned that online monitoring raises serious civil liberties and oversight questions.

If ASIO and the AFP now watch the chat rooms where teens are radicalised, is that protection or overreach?

Tell us what you think below.

#AusSight #auspol

warnings: Funding figure: ABC reports $76 million; the minister's 6 May 2026 release and AAP say $74 million over two years. The video and posts use $74 million.
The AFP '55 of 55' finding comes from Commissioner Krissy Barrett's Senate Estimates evidence as reported by The Nightly (29 Oct 2026); the transcript was not checked directly.
Burke's line that the social media ban is not enough on its own is reported by ABC News only.
Story involves minors and terrorism: keep replies factual; do not speculate about individual cases.
